title: Trump Says U.S. Will Stop Paying Israel After Year-End, Citing Deal With Netanyahu
excerpt: President Donald Trump said Tuesday the U.S. will stop providing funding to Israel after the end of this year, saying he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made a deal months ago.
content:
President Donald Trump said Tuesday that Washington will no longer provide funding to Israel after the end of this year, telling Fox News’ “Fox and Friends” that he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made a deal months ago to stop the payments.

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a year, and we made a deal months ago that we’re stopping,” Trump said, according to Reuters. “We’ve already agreed that by the end of this year we won’t be paying Israel. Now we’ll help Israel if they need it.”

The announcement came on Election Day, as voters across the country were casting ballots in the midterm elections. Reuters reported Trump’s remarks on Tuesday; the report did not publish the text of any agreement or include a confirmation from the Israeli government.

What this means — and what is still unclear

Taken at face value, the statement would end a $4 billion-a-year funding arrangement at year’s end, while leaving open future help “if they need it,” in Trump’s words. What remains unclear from the reporting so far is the form of the deal Trump described, whether it covers all forms of U.S. assistance, and how it would be carried out through Congress, which controls federal spending.

For readers in Webb County, the announcement is a reminder of how quickly a single presidential statement can reshape a long-running foreign-policy arrangement — and why the details, not just the headline, will determine what actually changes. Webb Watch 956 will update this story as the White House, Congress or the Israeli government provide further detail.

Update — November 11, 2026

Israel's government responded to Trump's announcement without confirming or denying a year-end cutoff. On Friday, November 6, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office posted a statement on X describing a move “from aid to partnership” and did not dispute Trump's account; a spokesperson for the prime minister said Netanyahu “has been working with President Trump to make the correct transition out from aid towards partnership and mutual investment.” The same day, Israeli President Isaac Herzog said the announcement “hit me like a bolt out of the blue,” noting that the current memorandum of understanding runs through 2028. U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee told Israel's Channel 12 on Thursday that he was unsure whether the aid would end immediately or at the end of 2028 and was seeking clarification. No written agreement, executive order, or congressional action setting out how the cutoff would work has been published, and the memorandum of understanding providing about $3.8 billion a year remains in force through September 2028.

Sources:

  • Reuters, “Trump says US will stop paying Israel after year-end” (Nov. 3, 2026)
  • Jewish Website, “Netanyahu’s office doesn’t deny Trump’s announcement of imminent halt to US military aid” (Nov. 6, 2026)
